# Tutorial 11: Machine Learning in R Part 2: Unsupervised {#sec-tute10}

Workshop 8 focussed on how we develop supervised machine learning models in R using the `tidymodels` R packages, and this can be used when our data has labels - where we know what each grouping should be. 

But what happens when we don't? 

This is when we used **Unsupervised** Machine Learning. You have probably come across many unsupervised machine learning applications in your research so far - Principle Components Analysis (PCA), Multidimensional Scaling (MDS), k-means clustering and hierarchical clustering are examples of unsupervised methods that try to discover patterns or structures in the data **without prior knowledge of the groupings**.
